match.reason: The closest card, Expanding brackets, covers expanding a single bracket but not expanding several brackets and then collecting like terms, and the other cards cover different ideas (binomial products, equations, perfect squares), so none teaches this point as it is.

draft.title: Expanding and collecting like terms
card: To expand, multiply every term inside the brackets by the number outside. So \(3(x + 2) = 3x + 6\).
A negative sign outside the brackets multiplies every term inside, and it changes each sign. So \(-2(x - 5) = -2x + 10\).
Like terms have the same pronumeral part. Add or subtract their coefficients: \(3x\) and \(-2x\) are like terms, but \(x\) and 7 are not.
Worked example
draft.remember: Expand each bracket first, with the sign that sits in front of it, then collect like terms.

a.why: The \(-2\) multiplies both terms: \(-2 \times x = -2x\) and \(-2 \times -5 = +10\). The tempting \(-2x - 10\) forgets that a negative times a negative is positive.

b.why: Expanding gives \(4x + 12 - 3x + 6\). Collecting like terms gives \(x + 18\). The tempting \(x + 6\) comes from writing \(-3 \times -2\) as \(-6\), so the second sign is wrong.
b.clue: Expand each bracket, then collect the \(x\) terms and the numbers.
